correctness.rationale: For all n>=40320, the digit contribution bound n-S5(n)>=36224-7162>0; for 1<=n<=40319 the image lies in [1,29008]. Hence finite enumeration of the 40319-state closed graph exhausts all periodic points. The reproducible exact-integer cycle tests agree under two distinct factorial-digit extraction algorithms and give seven fixed points plus the cycle 2114<->3401. Every one of 18 translated input orbits is checked term by term. The elementary digit-disjointness lemma and surjectivity construct a shifted interval of arbitrary length whose r-th images land inside one of the two verified translates of the complete periodic set. No inference from a finite sample to infinitely many inputs is made; the lifting proof establishes the quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The principal 2019 paper proved a conditional synchronizing-translate criterion and tabulated the fifth-power periodic points, but its unconditional consecutive-run theorem stopped at exponents at most four. New explicit translations for the entire nine-point fifth-power periodic set discharge the previously unverified hypothesis for targets 34 and 1058. Searches of exact statement and equivalent forms found no covering result. Relative priority remains subject to risks below.
residual_risks: The 2022 survey full text was not inspected; accessible text does not identify a competing theorem, but snippet-level evidence cannot rule one out.
An equivalent fifth-power synchronization result might exist in unindexed literature or under different terminology.
The proof inherits no claim of being the first discovery; scientific originality is assessed against the accessible evidence only.

value.rationale: The earlier principal paper explicitly highlighted the difficulty of its consecutive-run criterion for e>=5 because a genuine 2-cycle appears. These complete nine-state synchronization certificates cross that qualitative barrier for two distinct nontrivial fixed-point basins and yield infinite sequences of arbitrary lengths, not merely finite numerical instances. Both target basins are natural previously tabulated fixed-point classes. The result does not claim the unsolved standard 1-happy case, best possible translations, or density estimates.
